description: Hello we are 3 witty high school students looking for some fun. We like to eat In-n-out and also making learning accessible and fun for all.
summary:
Adventures with Oppy is a story based game where players play as NASA's Opportunity Rover. Oppy wakes up on Mars with her hardware scattered and buried in the sand, seeing only through black and white hazard cameras. Players explore the terrain and dig up each component by typing a real fact about it, while a CAD visual made in SolidWorks from NASA diagrams displays above. Recovering each part grants Oppy a new ability from driving, color vision, mineral scanning etc. Once all the parts are restored, Oppy puts all of her hardware to use through 4 minigames to understand what each part does.

The game’s storyline is designed to follow how Opportunity’s science team actually studied rocks. Digging up and using each component one by one, the player learns the function of each part and how they all contributed to the discovery of hematite blueberries, sign of past water on Mars!
details:
Game Mechanics:

When brainstorming game mechanics, we reflected on our own experiences with educational games. They often bordered either all learning that made it no different from reading a textbook, or too much gaming where the players could skip past the learning.

So for Adventures with Oppy, we intentionally designed the game mechanics to seamlessly integrate learning with fun gaming aspects so it doesn't have to be a compromise for one or the other. For example, we chose typing over reading to make learning more interactive and accessible than textbooks, while making sure players are reading and understanding every word.

In addition, we based the game mechanics off games that we personally find satisfying to play.

- Digging up Components: Inspired by Monkeytype, a typing test website
- Rock Abrasion Tool: Inspired by Osu!, a rythym game where you follow moving circles
- APXS: inspired by the reeling minigame in Fisch on Roblox, where you balance a bar inside a moving zone

Tools We Used:
- Game Development: Godot game engine, programmed in GDScript.
- CAD: We hand modeled every part on SolidWorks based on NASA photos and published papers on the development of the technologies. These serve visual learners, including us, who learn best by seeing how the forms interact and move.
- Website: in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, hosted on GitHub Pages. Built with AI assistance (AI disclosure in the footer of our website)

Our Goals:
Adventures with Oppy is designed to provide access to students grade 3-8 with little science background and any casual space enthusiasts to appreciate the engineering and impact of the complex hardware developed by NASA engineers.
